questions.q: What is the term for a person who is not a registered and licensed architect but practices architecture in violation of the law?
questions.n: Under Section 29 of RA 9266, individuals practicing without valid credentials are subject to criminal charges and fines.

questions.q: What is the name of the 'Professional Tax' paid annually by an architect to the city or municipality where they practice?
questions.n: The PTR is a local government requirement for all professionals to legally offer their services in a specific jurisdiction.

questions.q: Under RA 9266, which body has the power to suspend or revoke the Certificate of Registration of an architect?
o: The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture (PRBOA)
questions.n: The PRBOA is the government body under the PRC tasked with the regulation and administrative discipline of the profession.

questions.q: What is the 'Continuing Professional Development' (CPD) requirement for the renewal of an architect’s PRC ID?
questions.n: The traditional requirement for a 3-year renewal cycle for RLAs is 45 units, though this is subject to current PRC resolutions.

questions.q: What is the minimum fine for any person who forces an architect to perform service without a written contract?
questions.n: The law protects architects by mandating a minimum fine of 200k for those who coerce professional services without a legal contract.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear width for a door leaf in a residential dwelling according to the NBC?
questions.n: The NBC sets 0.70m as the minimum clear width for residential doors to allow for safe passage.

questions.q: For a staircase in a residential building (Group A), what is the maximum height of a 'Riser'?
questions.n: The NBC allows a maximum riser height of 200mm for residential structures (Group A).

questions.q: What is the minimum width of a 'Tread' (run) for a staircase in a residential building?
questions.n: The minimum tread depth is 200mm to ensure enough surface area for safe stepping.

questions.q: What is the minimum dimension for a 'Ventilating Opening' (window) in a room intended for human habitation?
questions.n: To ensure adequate natural light and air, windows must be at least 10% of the room's total floor area.

questions.q: In a basement or windowless story, what is the minimum dimension of the 'Emergency Egress Window'?
questions.n: This specific size ensures that a person (including emergency responders with gear) can pass through.

questions.q: What is the minimum area for an accessible 'Water Closet' (toilet) stall according to BP 344?
questions.n: This dimension allows for a wheelchair to maneuver alongside the toilet fixture for transfer.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear width of an accessible 'Parking Slot'?
questions.n: The 3.70m width includes the standard 2.50m stall plus a 1.20m access aisle.

questions.q: What is the maximum height of a 'Light Switch' from the floor to be reachable for a person in a wheelchair?
questions.n: BP 344 specifies that switches and controls should be within a reach range of 0.90m to 1.20m.

questions.q: What is the minimum length of a 'Grab Bar' placed beside a toilet?
questions.n: The grab bar must be at least 0.80m long to ensure the user has a continuous grip surface.

questions.q: What is the required length of a 'Level Area' or landing at the top and bottom of a ramp?
questions.n: A 1.50m landing ensures that a wheelchair has enough room to stop safely without rolling back.

questions.q: During the Bidding or Negotiation Phase, the architect assists the owner in preparing what specific set of documents?
o: Forms for Invitation to Bid and Instruction to Bidders
questions.n: The architect prepares the technical and procedural paperwork required to solicit and evaluate bids.

questions.q: In the Construction Phase, how often is the architect expected to visit the site under Regular Design Services?
o: Only at the beginning and end
questions.n: Under regular services, the architect visits periodically to check progress and ensure general compliance with the design.

questions.q: What is the percentage of the architect’s fee paid upon the completion of the Contract Document Phase?
questions.n: The completion of the CDs entitles the architect to 50% of the fee for that phase, reaching 85% cumulatively.

questions.q: What is the 'Retention' fee percentage usually held by the owner from the contractor's progress billings?
questions.n: Retention is a fund kept by the owner to ensure the contractor finishes the work and corrects any early defects.

questions.q: If the architect is tasked to provide 'Full-time Supervision,' which SPP document governs this additional service?
questions.n: This document specifies the duties and fees for an architect or firm providing full-time site supervision.

questions.q: What is the maximum allowable length of a 'Dead-End Corridor' in a building with a sprinkler system?
questions.n: With a sprinkler system, the Fire Code allows for longer dead ends as the risk of fire spread is reduced.

questions.q: What is the minimum width of a 'Fire Escape Stair' for an occupant load of less than 10?
questions.n: The Fire Code allows a reduced width of 600mm only for very small occupant loads (less than 10).

questions.q: What is the minimum thickness of a 'Firewall' made of solid masonry according to the code?
questions.n: Solid masonry of 150mm provides the necessary fire resistance rating required for boundary walls.

questions.q: What is the minimum width of a 'Stairway' in a building with an occupant load of more than 50?
questions.n: For buildings where more than 50 people use the stairs, a minimum of 1.12m is required for egress flow.

questions.q: What is the minimum 'Landing' width for a fire exit stair?
o: Must be at least as wide as the stair
Half the width of the stair
questions.n: The landing must maintain the full width of the stair to prevent bottlenecks during an emergency.
